notes:
1. Correction: the card object I gave for pumped_hydro_storage still says "cost": 24. It should be 18, as the reason, the anchor check and the printed text say. Use 18.

2. Most changes lower prices. At the anchors, almost every Power income card read 0.9-1.1 at tier 1 and 1.1-1.5 at tier 2, so most of the fixes are lower credit costs rather than new effects. Lower prices cut against "credits pile up". The real disagreement is that the anchors value income and energy below what the printed prices assumed. If you would rather keep prices high, the anchors (+1 energy income 14, +1 credit income 4) are what has to move.

3. Per-tag income programs, across all six tags. Capacity Market's shape (10 credits, needs 2) reads 0.67-0.89 at 3-4 tags. I took Power's to 5 credits; Research Royalties and the other tags' versions have the same problem and should move together, or the rule "one shape for one job" breaks.

4. The liberate capstones. The 080 design prices them at their own value, which is about 1.0. Your tier-2 band of 1.8-2.5 forced The Nuclear Option down to 4 credits plus 1 antimatter, and Power to the People to 6 credits plus 4 energy (chips dropped). That is a family-wide call for you. If you approve it, the other capstones (Hostile Buyout, Forensic Audit, Root Access, Peacekeeping Mission, Popular Uprising) need the same treatment. player-cards.md's capstone table ("power + chips", "needs 3") and economy.md (Dyson Swarm Tranche named as an energy-cost card, Tidal Barrage's line) would go stale.

5. Antimatter at 7 inflates Positron Storage Ring (2.18 with it, 1.46 without). An antimatter income of 1 a round yields 3-4 antimatter over a game, but only about 4 cards spend one. I kept the card. If you accept card-pricing's note that antimatter is really worth about 3, its income should become something else.

6. Tidal Barrage is a tag payoff, so its tier-1 ceiling is above 1.5 on purpose: 1.83 at 6 Power tags (+3 energy income). That breaks card-pricing's "no card above +2 energy income", which I read as superseded by your ruling 5.

7. Assumptions behind the checks:
- Substation Hub assumes about 0.7 teammate Power plays a round. Its sizing depends on table size.
- Action buildings are counted at 3.5 uses with no 0.7 share.
- A node is 4 (values.json), or 6 if placed free.
- A gift is 0.75 of face.
- Grid Census and Beamed Power Constellation assume 5-8 nodes.

8. No 30-50 credit late-game card. At these anchors, nothing Power can print at 30-50 credits reaches 1.8. Income late in the game counts few rounds, and a removal is 5 each. I spent the new slot on throughput instead (Fusion Research Campus, plus Grid Analytics Desk turning spare energy into cards). If you want a late-game card worth 30-50 credits, the anchors for liberation and sway need to rise, or that card is a liberation plus a sweep.

9. Deck and section shape. The deck stays at 154: Transmission Corridor cut, Fusion Research Campus added. The new card needs configs/baseline.json and `shared_row.py`. The section ends at 16 tier 1 and 8 tier 2, with 14 programs, 7 buildings and 3 events (was 15, 6, 3).

notes:
1) ENGINE BLOCKER for rulings 1-2: crates/aic-core/src/modules/effects/feasible.rs uses all() over the effects, so a program or event is not offered unless EVERY targeted op has a target. add_tokens (not here) needs a Capital building, cash_out needs Capital, jam needs a counterable threat of its type, and build_factory needs a site. So the new Payroll Automation, Capital Injection and Collateralized Grid (and Deep State Ledger, Supply Chain Audit and Antitrust Action today) still cannot be played without a target, whatever their main effect. To make feeders 'useful alone', add_tokens and cash_out (and arguably a typed jam beside an income or gain) should join the only_these / one_acts group, which vetoes a card only when it would do nothing at all. This is needed before any screen.
2) Value-table disagreements: chips are 1.5 in values.json but 3 at the anchor, which doubles Joint Fabrication Pact's and Parts Exchange's worth. Credit income at 4 a point makes every plain income program read about 1.0 at its old price (Robotic Foundry, Gigafactory, Payroll), hence the reprices. A help card's gift is counted at 0.75 of face (values.json other_gain). Standing counters (auto_counter about 13) cannot reach the tier-2 band at any price.
3) Shared shapes: Economies of Scale is the cross-tag 'per-tag income program, needs 2, 10 credits'. At the anchors that shape reads 0.9-1.1 at 4-5 tags, so I repriced Industry's to 7 credits; the other five tags' twins probably need the same. Cutting Market Stabilization Board leaves Autonomous Defense Grid (Cyber) as the only standing counter, so player-cards.md's 'Industry and Cyber keep a standing automatic counter' needs an edit. Retained Earnings' price rose because its own play fills the threshold of 4 at once.
4) Kept on purpose above the band: Vertical Monopoly reads 2.5 at 5 Industry tags and 2.9 at 6 or more (Matt's 'broken when well played' engine). Arcology Foundry is just under the tier-2 band (1.75); I kept it.
5) Mix: 2 cut (Liquidity Event, an event; Market Stabilization Board, a tier-2 building) and 2 new (Supplier Network, a tier-1 building; Wartime Retooling, a tier-1 program). Industry stays at 25, with tier 2 going from 7 to 6. Supplier Network puts draw inside a when trigger's then, which the grammar allows (instant player ops), but no card does yet: check face.rs and value.rs for a draw in a trigger. Plant Overdrive's card object has a typo: its tag must stay 'industry', not 'power'. Corrected op: {"op":"gain_per_tag","resource":"energy","tag":"industry","per":1}.
6) Each change keeps a one-reading face. All new numbers sit at the anchors' tier-1 band (1.07-1.50) or tier-2 band (1.64-2.5). No removal cards are in Industry, so the reach ruling touches none here.

notes:
I reviewed all 27 Science cards: 9 kept, 16 changed, 2 cut, 2 new. The section stays at 27 cards: tier 1 goes from 20 to 21 and tier 2 from 7 to 6, with buildings and programs one-for-one. I edited no files.

How I priced:
- **Engines** are counted over 3.5 rounds (the middle of the 3-4 the brief gives). Each engine's fire on its own play counts too, because the rules say a building counts itself.
- **A Dataset** is worth 3 (the feed_datasets rate in values.json). That matches Telemetry Archive's new rate of 3 insight per 4 Datasets.
- **A megaproject cube** is worth 6 (values.json). The Researcher's Grant power is a plain route at 3 credits a cube.

Findings and flags:
1. **Telemetry Archive was the worst outlier, at 3.3.** Its 2 Datasets when built plus the 2 from its own Science play fill the At 4 threshold at once (6 insight, worth 24, for a 20 pay). After that it paid 3 insight, worth 12, per Science card. The fix halves the reward and raises the price to 15.
2. **The ratio cap pushes engines' build draws to two fires' worth** (2 cards on Citation Engine and Grad Student Pool), and Citation Engine's price up to 20. Both readings counted the self-fire.
3. **Synthetic Data Forge with Dataset Scraper is a deliberate two-card combo above the cap.** The Forge keeps its tokens, so 2 Datasets add 2 insight to every later cash, about 3.1 on Scraper's pay. That fits the "looks broken when well played" direction, but Matt should confirm it. Telemetry Archive is the at-rate target.
4. **Forensic Audit reads 0.88 on the anchors, far under the tier-2 band.** The anchor of 45 for a city cannot carry tier 2: reaching 1.8 would need the card to cost about 1 credit. Every liberate capstone (18-42 credits) has the same gap. Either the city anchor is low (the plain route costs about 100 and play is near 50), or the capstones are exempt from the band as credit sinks. I kept it for Matt to rule on rather than repricing one capstone alone.
5. **A 30-50 credit card cannot reach the tier-2 band (1.8 or more).** It would need 83-125 of value, which only liberation-sized effects reach. So the late-game card, Moonshot Grant (28 credits), is a dear tier 1 at 1.28, as ruling 5 allows.
6. **Research cubes are worth about 4, not 3.** The cube converter (1 cube for 1 insight) gives every cube at least the insight anchor. Sample Repository's cube income was effectively an insight income, which is why it was cut.
7. **Cuts leave stale references.** These need cleaning up in the same change:
   - Data Licensing Deal is card-grammar.md's example for the `place_tokens` trigger, so the trigger has no card left and the example needs replacing.
   - Both cut ids appear in `crates/aic-core/src/tests/engine.rs` and `tests/researcher.rs`.
   - Both also appear in `configs/agents/strategies.json`, `docs/card-pricing-notes.json`, `docs/rules/ai-powers.md` and `docs/rules/economy.md`.
   - player-cards.md's "five tier-1 and one tier-2" niche count is still right, because Open-Weights Release stays.
8. **Two numbers the board-state brief doesn't size.** Predictive Modeling now delays 2 threats; it was 3, which may exceed the threats usually up. Open-Weights Release clears 4 markers. I couldn't measure either.
9. **Orbital Observatory Array (1.75) and Recursive Self-Improvement (1.7) are kept just under the tier-2 band** on purpose. Interdisciplinary Institute (2.32) and Foundation Model Campus (2.05) are in band.
10. **Moonshot Grant prints `project_cube` without `station`**, so any incomplete megaproject counts. Late in the game it can be dead if every megaproject is complete. Six cubes on an 8-cube card is meant as a big push, not a disguised "complete it".

notes:
The Diplomacy section: 26 cards → 25. Truth Commission and Planetary Referendum are cut and Envoy Briefings is added, so the deck goes 154 → 153. Tier-2 count goes 8 → 7.

1. Engine blocker for ruling 2. In crates/aic-core/src/modules/effects/feasible.rs, the `Op::AddTokens { kind, .. }` arm (not `here`) vetoes the whole card when the seat has no token card of that kind. As things stand, the new Manifesto Leak is never offered without a Follower building, so it is still useless alone. Every tag's feeder has the same problem. Fix: treat AddTokens like Draw and OtherGain in that file's `only_these` group: veto it only when it is the card's only effect.

2. A play-feasibility catch. Every targeted effect on a card must have a target (`.all`). That is why I didn't pair a removal with a cleanse on Liberation Accords: the card would be dead unless both targets were present.

3. Reconciliation Office now has a `draw` inside a `when` trigger. content.rs checks trigger `then` ops at Slot::Player, and Draw is a Player op, but no card has printed this before. Check its face text and how the agents value it.

4. Cards below band on purpose:
   - Hostile Buyout reads 1.29 at tier 2. It is the dear late-game credit card Matt asked for. Late credits are idle (25-63 a seat at game end), so at about 0.5 a late credit it reads about 2.
   - Peace Dividend reads 0.89-1.11. That is the shared per-tag income shape across all six tags, so any fix belongs to all of them, not just this card.
   - Back-Channel Talks reads 1.44 only if 3 corrupted factories are in reach. That count isn't in the board-state brief; if it is usually 1, the card is weak and often unplayable.

5. Value-table disagreements:
   - values.json prices an ambassador removal at 2.2 and clear_city at 2 per ambassador, against the anchor's 5. The agents will undervalue every removal card here by about half.
   - Sway at 4 is cheap near a tip: a Unity tip is 2 x players, and the Undecided pool is 4 x players. I kept printed sway at 6 or less for that reason.
   - Followers have no anchor. I used values feed_followers 2.5; Popular Uprising pays about 7.5 a Follower toward a liberation.

6. Out of my section but tagged Diplomacy: Diplomatic Expulsion (8 in one country, 10 credits) and Martial Cordon (10 in one country) are Security primaries. They are exactly the cases Matt flagged; Liberation Accords now owns the 6-in-reach tier-2 job. Whoever fixes them shouldn't repeat it.

1. ENGINE BLOCKER FOR RULING 2. In `crates/aic-core/src/modules/effects/feasible.rs`, AddTokens without `here` is a strict veto: a card whose feeder has no Agent building can't be played at all, main effect included. Recruit Operatives and Deep State Ledger (and every other tag's feeders under ruling 2) stay dead alone until AddTokens joins the list that only vetoes a card that would otherwise do nothing (beside Harden, MoveOne, Draw). Without that change ruling 2 isn't met, whatever the card text says.

2. Removals and the same veto. Any program or event with a removal plus another effect can't be played when the removal has no target. That is why every troop-only card in reach is a cut or a cheap event, and why the mixed cards use `damage` (ambassadors OR troops, one hex) or ambassadors in reach. Troops are 0-1 a country, so I moved most Security removal to ambassadors in reach. Troops stay on Breach and Clear and Garrison Command (in reach, 1-2), Kinetic Interdiction (3 in one country, the deliberate tier-2 sweep), Peacekeeping Mission's twist and Counterinsurgency's choice. They feed Security Contractor HQ. The tier-2 one-country sweeps left are Kinetic Interdiction (troops), Martial Cordon (7 ambassadors) and Peacekeeping Mission (its city's country).

3. Value-table disagreements with the anchors:
- Troop removal is 11 in values.json (7 in one country) against the anchor's 5; the heuristic reads about 20. At 5, HQ's 10 a troop is a 3x boost. I kept HQ because troops are scarce.
- For cordon I used about 2 arrivals stopped x 5 = 10; values.json says 5. Hardpoint Lockdown reads 1.0 at values and 1.33 at mine.
- I valued an Agent at about 4: Safehouse spends 2 for 3 cards, and Directorate's 3 fill a 15 fire. values.json feed_agents is 2. At 2 the feeders' with-target ratios fall about 0.3.
- Typed jam: I used about 5 for jam 6 on military (values: 0.7 x 6 = 4.2).

The whole liberate family prices under the tier-2 band at the 45 anchor: Hostile Buyout 42, Root Access 40, Forensic Audit 27 plus cubes. Defense Appropriations at 1.11 is the shared per-tag shape (10 cr, needs 2) in every tag, kept for consistency. Kinetic Interdiction now costs 0 credits (paid in energy and antimatter).
